findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's long-lived access key would allow full control of compute, storage and serverless resources account-wide, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via lambda:CreateFunction/ec2:RunInstances with a more privileged role.

A static, non-rotating IAM access key is provisioned for a user holding account-wide wildcard permissions; its plaintext secret is also persisted in Terraform state because no pgp_key is supplied, so anyone with read access to the state backend obtains working privileged credentials. Temporary STS credentials from an assumable role should be used instead.

The svc_deploy_key_material output exports access key material and is not marked sensitive, so the value can appear in plan/apply logs, CI output, and is readable by any consumer of the remote state outputs. Note that because no pgp_key is set, encrypted_secret will be empty, but the output pattern is still a credential-disclosure path.

A standalone IAM user is used for deployment automation with no permissions_boundary and no MFA requirement to constrain the account-wide privileges granted to it, so any credential compromise is unbounded. An assumable role with temporary credentials would limit the blast radius.
